sections.title: Letter cappa
paragraphs: The letter (cappa) /ˈkappa/ makes the clear sound /k/. Hear it in the word (kiwi) /ˈki.wi/, which means kiwi. This letter has only one sound in Italian. It appears almost only in words taken from other languages.

sections.title: Pronouncing the letter
paragraphs: Raise the back of your tongue against the soft back of your mouth roof. Stop the air for a moment. Then release the air suddenly without any breathy puff. Place a hand before your mouth. You should feel no burst of air when you make this crisp click.

sections.title: Spelling and use
paragraphs: You see (cappa) /ˈkappa/ in foreign borrowings and international loanwords. In these words, it always makes the sound /k/. You can hear it in (kamikaze) /kamiˈkad.dze/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: In English words like kite, you release a small puff of breath. Italian never adds this breathy air. Make the stop sharp and clean, closer to the k in skin than the k in key. Hold back your breath completely.
